Convert MIDI to MP3

What this does

A MIDI to MP3 converter turns note data into audible audio: MIDI stores no sound, so the file has to be rendered through a soundfont, and this page does that render inside your browser with the General MIDI FluidR3 bank. This converter renders with the General MIDI FluidR3 soundfont in your browser, which is why a piano track plays as a GM piano rather than your DAW's sampled piano.

Open the converter with the format selected

How to convert

  1. Choose a .mid, .midi or .kar file.
  2. Set the output to MP3.
  3. Convert, then Download.

How long does MIDI to MP3 take?

About seven seconds for a short single-track file: most of that is the 14 MB soundfont download, which the browser caches for the next run. Long orchestral scores take proportionally longer to render.

Is the MP3 lossless?

No. MIDI carries notes and program numbers, not audio. The MP3 is a lossy render of General MIDI instruments, so any custom instrument the original arrangement used is replaced by its GM preset.

What you get

All tracks are mixed into one stereo MP3. The sound is determined by General MIDI program numbers. If the original file depends on custom instruments, the result will sound different from what you hear in your DAW.

FAQ

Why does it sound different from my DAW?

The render uses the General MIDI FluidR3 soundfont. Any custom instrument in the original arrangement is replaced by the matching GM preset.

Are all tracks mixed together?

Yes — the output is one mixed audio file, not a stem export.

Does it accept .kar files?

Yes, .kar (MIDI karaoke) files are accepted; the lyrics are not rendered into the audio.
